questions.prompt:
How should the API respond to this practical HTTP request?
POST /users  body={"email":"ada@example.com","age":20}
options: Keep all state in a global variable and skip authentication.
Ignore HTTP status codes and present failures as successful responses.
Return the same response to every request without checking its data.
questions.explanation: This is the expected behavior for `POST /users  body={"email":"ada@example.com","age":20}`. 200 OK; JSON: {"email":"ada@example.com","age":20}

questions.prompt: Which design principle is correct for this topic?
options: A Pydantic model parses JSON into typed Python fields and rejects incompatible data before the endpoint runs.
Keep all state in a global variable and skip authentication.
Return the same response to every request without checking its data.
Ignore HTTP status codes and present failures as successful responses.
questions.answer: A Pydantic model parses JSON into typed Python fields and rejects incompatible data before the endpoint runs.
questions.explanation: A Pydantic model parses JSON into typed Python fields and rejects incompatible data before the endpoint runs. In Pydantic v2, `str | None` permits null; `= None` also makes the field optional. Type and requiredness are separate decisions.

questions.prompt: What changes if the important part shown in the lesson is omitted?
options: Return the same response to every request without checking its data.
Ignore HTTP status codes and present failures as successful responses.
Without a body model, the input shape is undocumented and relies on repeated manual checks.
Keep all state in a global variable and skip authentication.
questions.answer: Without a body model, the input shape is undocumented and relies on repeated manual checks.
questions.explanation: Without a body model, the input shape is undocumented and relies on repeated manual checks. POST/PUT requests often carry new or changed data in a JSON body. A Pydantic model states field types and constraints in one place; FastAPI parses and validates the model before calling the endpoint.

questions.prompt: Which action best prevents the common mistake from this lesson?
options: Return the same response to every request without checking its data.
Ignore HTTP status codes and present failures as successful responses.
Submit the expected body in `/docs`, then remove a field and observe the automatic 422 response.
Keep all state in a global variable and skip authentication.
questions.answer: Submit the expected body in `/docs`, then remove a field and observe the automatic 422 response.
questions.explanation: Submit the expected body in `/docs`, then remove a field and observe the automatic 422 response. Never trust client values. Model validation does not replace business rules, authorization, or protection of private data.
